title: Directions, ensembles and one-shot experience
subtitle: Muon spectral margins · Multi-epoch ensembles · GS1 · GAE
intro: Three main readings examine attention directions under Muon, ensemble-dependent stopping with fixed data, and baselines from one rollout per task. Five new-paper briefs and two version observations follow. The GAE classic develops telescoping sums and bias.

articles.authors: Shengwei Wu · Yixuan Yang · Gao Huang · Song Li
articles.title: Learn outputs first, then spectral max-margin attention
articles.evidence: Read model, Algorithm 1, Theorems 1–2 and assumptions; appendix proofs not checked line by line

blocks.text: A one-layer softmax-attention model directly optimizes combined output W₁ and attention W₂ matrices. W₁ is trained on singleton contexts, then frozen while W₂ learns; both start at zero.[1]

blocks.label: q is the final token, x* the correct token, and 𝒳⁻ the other context tokens; γ*=1/R* [1]

blocks.text: Assume orthonormal token embeddings, bijective labels h, a correct token at least as frequent as competitors, and common separability. After sufficient preprocessing, with fixed momentum and sufficiently small η₀:[1]

blocks.tex: \eta_t=\eta_0(t+1)^{-1/2},\quad 0<\mathcal L_T(W_{2,t})-\ell_T^*\le C_1t^{C_2}e^{-C_3\sqrt t},\quad 0\le\gamma_* -\rho_2(W_{2,t}/\|W_{2,t}\|_{\rm op})\le C_4\frac{1+\log t}{\sqrt t}

blocks.text: Exact-polar, full-batch, staged optimization of combined matrices does not establish the same guarantee for jointly trained deep Transformers or finite-step Newton–Schulz.[1]

articles.title: Allocate fixed-data compute between time and members
articles.evidence: Read section 2, section 3.5 and Appendix A.2 budget/fitting setup; DMFT proofs not fully checked

blocks.text: Repeated FineWeb training can produce U-shaped validation loss; logit ensembles delay stopping. Theory separates error correlations using shared data and independent random-feature projections.[2]

blocks.label: Squared-error identity: E is ensemble size; self/cross denote expected error products for identical/distinct members [2]
Left: empirical LM fit. Right: common 40-epoch budget; P is unique tokens and N counted parameters per member [2]

blocks.text: Four 85M counted-parameter members match one twice-wide model’s proxy budget, excluding embeddings, output head and scalar gains. RF allocation instead charges each ensemble to its own stopping time.[2]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Shared-data error remains. The RF squared-error identity differs from cross-entropy approximations; parameter-token budgets omit ensemble inference overhead and are not measured wall-clock costs.[2]

articles.paper: Meta-memorization and memorization scaling laws in transformers
articles.authors: Alex Nguyen · Kenneth A. Norman · Gautam Reddy
articles.title: Brief | Learning to memorize random sequences faster
articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-11-01 00:43 EDT · v1; delayed catch-up outside window
articles.evidence: Based on abstract; full text not closely read

blocks.text: Random binary sequences remove semantic structure. Reported capacity grows roughly linearly with parameters, while memorization rate grows as a power of training time; prior memorization accelerates new-sequence storage. Mechanistic attribution and transfer to natural-language knowledge require further checks.[5]

blocks.text: Ten 5.8M–1.97B encoders use 25,067–79,910 EEG hours across 23 tasks. Capacity-dependent data saturation and declining transfer can coexist with improving pretraining loss. Linear probing, full fine-tuning and shared-Qwen readout results are distinct.[6]

blocks.text: Million- and billion-parameter models differ after fine-tuning on transformed languages; semantic coherence distinguishes structural and semantic perturbations. This is an empirical size effect, not an established universal power law; pretraining priors may contribute.[7]

classic.paper: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation
classic.authors: John Schulman · Philipp Moritz · Sergey Levine · Michael I. Jordan · Pieter Abbeel
classic.title: How λ lets bootstrap error reach the actor
classic.dateNote: First posted 2015-06-08; read v5 (2016-09-09), sections 2–4 and experiments; ICLR 2016
classic.evidence: Read γ-justness, GAE derivation and control experiments; error expansion is our explanatory algebra
classic.question: For equal critic MSE, how should λ control actor bias when errors concentrate in states with large score norms?

blocks.text: REINFORCE (1992) uses full returns; TD(λ) combines bootstrapping and multistep returns. GAE applies this structure to advantages and combines it with TRPO for continuous control.[10,11]
Consider an on-policy episode ending at T, reward rₜ and fixed critic V with V(sT)=0; γ and λ lie between zero and one. The paper’s original objective is undiscounted; γ also controls variance.[10]

blocks.label: Exponential multistep mixture yields a backward recurrence [10]
Our finite-episode expansion, with eT=0; current −eₜ is a baseline, while future errors may depend on the action
Paper γ-justness: any fixed V; with V=Vπ,γ, every λ is γ-just [10]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: γ-justness targets the paper’s gγ, not automatically the undiscounted gradient. A time limit is not a true terminal state and need not have zero bootstrap; control experiments do not quantify LLM gains.[10]
